attempts.label: CRCNS:nac-1
attempts.entry_title: Threat and bidirectional valence signaling in the nucleus accumbens core (Ray et al. 2022)
attempts.summary: The behavioral findings and most of the neural population findings held up, but the cluster counts and the reward analyses did not. Rats discriminated danger, uncertainty and safety, and the Threat Inhibited, Danger Excited and Bidirectional Valence firing patterns reproduced, though several effect sizes differed. The five-cluster counts and the Threat Excited and Non-Selective results failed, because the paper's population labels are not deposited. Reward and nose poke cessation findings failed, since recordings are paused between trials. Pre-surgery acquisition could not be tested, and the dataset has 90 sessions, not 95.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Ray, Moaddab and McDannald (2022) on CRCNS data set nac-1, which holds 368 nucleus accumbens core single units recorded from seven female rats during Pavlovian fear discrimination, with the session's cue, shock, pellet and nose poke times. It tests the behavior during recording, the cue-responsive screen, the k-means populations, their firing and waveform characteristics, cue firing, firing similarity, tuning curves, the fear output and exaggerated threat regressions, and reward and nose poke cessation firing. The pre-surgery sessions and the paper's population labels are not in the data set.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Ray et al. (2022) from CRCNS nac-1

outcomes.notes: The data set holds 368 unit files from 7 rats (ac01, ac03 to ac08), as the paper says, but from 90 distinct sessions (rat and date; one behavior program per rat and date), not 95. Counting distinct rows of 16 suppression ratios, as mainAnalysis.m does, gives 84. No unit is deposited twice (no identical spike trains, no session and unit name used twice) and no two sessions share event times. Sessions per rat are ac01 17, ac03 17, ac04 10, ac05 17, ac06 16, ac07 7 and ac08 6; the paper's per-rat counts (Extended Data Figure 1-1) were not available to compare. The criterion's tolerance is zero for each count and it names no partial outcome, so the session count makes it not reproduced.

Reading (b) (shock and omission trials as two cues) finds 211 units from 81 sessions, at least 7 per rat, all within tolerance. Reading (a) finds 219 units (above 193 +- 19.3) from 82 sessions, with 6 in rat ac07. The authors' own procedure (rates floored to integers, as cubeScriptPR25.m stores them, pooled uncertainty) finds exactly 193 units from 82 sessions, at least 7 per rat. With onsets moved 10 s earlier (inside the recorded segment and before any cue), 25.8% of the 368 units pass reading (a), 29.1% reading (b) and 21.5% the script's screen, against 59.5%, 57.3% and 52.4% at the true onsets; six uncorrected tests at 0.05 would pass about 26% by chance. The paper states no chance level. The later claims use the script's 193 units, an assumption stated with fig2-five-clusters.
deviations: A test whose differences have no variance gives no p-value and does not count, as MATLAB ttest returns NaN and mainAnalysis.m sets it to 0.

outcomes.notes: The data set holds one file per recorded unit, from the 18 recording dates only, a precomputed cube built from them and the authors' scripts. The authors' preRecordingBehavior.m reads the pre-surgery sessions from a folder (AC Group Data) that is not deposited.

Under every reading the cue effect holds (F(2,12) 52.6 to 57.4, p < 1e-5), the three means are within tolerance (danger minus uncertainty 0.20 to 0.22, uncertainty minus safety 0.47 to 0.48, danger minus safety 0.67 to 0.70) and the danger minus uncertainty and danger minus safety CIs exclude zero. The uncertainty minus safety CI excludes zero only with all 90 sessions and 0/0 ratios read as 0 (median bounds over 50 seeds [0.012, 0.599], excluding zero in 68% of seeds); under the other readings its lower bound is -0.05 to -0.17, as rat ac01 has a difference of 0.15. With 0/0 set to 1 (the scripts' handling) and the 82 sessions, F(2,12) = 57.41 and the means 0.21, 0.47 and 0.69 equal the paper's exactly. The paper's printed CIs match the bootstrap-t quantiles added to the mean without reflection ([0.36, 1.03] against [0.35, 1.03]). With seed 1001 that CI is [0.04, 0.59]. Judged again over five seeds, it reproduces in 3 of 5 with the analytic SE and 2 of 5 with the inner bootstrap SE. With the non-reflected form every CI excludes zero under every reading and seed, and the claim is reproduced under all six readings.
deviations: Each rat's value is the mean over its sessions, as mainAnalysis.m averages the session rows of each rat (cueR.cerInd).
With seven rats the bound near zero moves with the bootstrap seed; the CI is judged on the median bounds over 50 seeds, a tie-break the criterion does not give.

Bootstrap CIs are the standard (reflected) studentized interval with the analytic standard error in each of 1000 resamples. The notebook's CI section judges the claim again with the non-reflected form (which matches the paper's Figure 1G CIs), with the inner bootstrap SE of MATLAB bootci (100 resamples) and with five seeds.

The outcome rests on one reading, all 90 sessions with 0/0 suppression ratios read as 0, judged on the median bounds over 50 seeds. That is not the authors' handling. With 0/0 set to 1, as the scripts do and as fig1h-poke-rate-unrelated assumes because it gives the paper's F exactly, the uncertainty minus safety CI contains zero in every one of the 50 seeds with the standard interval, in both session sets (median lower bounds -0.125 with the 82 sessions and -0.084 with the 90), and the claim is not reproduced with that interval.

outcomes.notes: With 0/0 suppression ratios set to 1 (the scripts' handling, which gives the paper's F(2,12) = 57.41 exactly) or left out, no correlation of baseline poke rate with danger, uncertainty or safety suppression or with danger minus safety has p < 0.05, in the 82 or the 90 sessions (largest |R| 0.49, smallest p 0.26). With 0/0 read as 0, baseline poke rate correlates with danger suppression in the 82 sessions (R = 0.76, p = 0.048) and not in the 90 (R = 0.73, p = 0.063).
deviations: A 0/0 suppression ratio (no pokes in baseline or cue) is set to 1, as cubeScriptPR25.m and mainAnalysis.m do (cer.cue(isnan(cer.cue)) = 1); the claims file names leaving it out or 0, and the Methods are silent. Assumed because the scripts' handling reproduces the paper's ANOVA exactly; the outcome is the same when 0/0 trials are left out, and differs when they are read as 0.

outcomes.notes: Danger minus safety suppression correlates with safety suppression across the seven rats under every reading (R = -0.978 to -0.986, p from 4.5e-5 to 1.4e-4; the paper R = -0.98, p = 1.41e-4).

No reading gives the five counts within tolerance. With N4 and the most frequent of 100 starts the centroids show the five patterns (smallest cosine to the templates 0.79) with 6, 28, 45, 89 and 25 units (Threat Excited, Threat Inhibited, Danger Excited, Bidirectional Valence, Non-Selective); N2 gives 7, 27, 44, 91 and 24 (smallest cosine 0.77) and N4 with the best of 100 starts 46, 28, 27, 86 and 6 (0.73). The script normalization's best partition (9, 25, 34, 89 and 36; 0.66) and N1 most frequent (0.65) come close; the other readings give partitions whose centroids do not show the patterns (smallest cosine 0.30 or below), and firing in Hz groups units by rate. The normalized partitions are unstable (each found in 1 to 3 of 100 starts; the most frequent partition in Hz in 19), and the mean distance falls steadily from k = 1 to 7. On the 219 units of screen reading (a) the counts are 47, 36, 80, 45 and 11.
deviations: The 193 cue-responsive units are those of the authors' screen in mainAnalysis.m on the floored rates of cubeScriptPR25.m (paired ttest, uncertainty rows 5 to 12), the only procedure that gives the paper's 193 units and 82 sessions; the Methods do not mention flooring.
Clusters are named by a one-to-one match of centroids to pattern templates coding the Results' descriptions (largest summed cosine); the claims file names the patterns, not a rule.
Starts are scikit-learn k-means++ starts with fixed seeds; the script's single MATLAB start after rng(1) cannot be repeated.

findings.statement: The data set holds 368 units from 90 sessions (rat and date, one behavior program each), where the paper and the data description say 95 sessions.
The eight pre-surgery fear discrimination sessions of Figure 1C are not deposited; the authors' preRecordingBehavior.m reads them from a folder that is not in the data set.

The paper's population (k-means cluster) labels are not deposited. The authors' mainAnalysis.m computes them with one MATLAB k-means start after rng(1), which cannot be repeated outside MATLAB, and the reproduced clustering is unstable and does not give the paper's counts, so every population finding rests on a reproduced partition.

The data description does not say which EVT channel holds which event, nor that the cue channels change with the behavior program; only cubeScriptPR25.m gives the map (EVT01 shock, EVT02 pellet, EVT13 poke, cue channels per program a to f).

The recording is paused between trials, so the files hold spikes, pokes and pellets only from 20 s before each cue onset to about 33.5 s after it (inter-spike gaps of about 200 s). The data description does not say so, and the paper's inter-trial interval analyses can use only these windows.
The data description says NAcccube.poke.base is the nose poke rate 2 s before the cue; in cube.mat it is the rate over the 20 s before the cue (pokes per min), in all 368 units.

The authors' scripts differ from the Methods in ways that change results. Firing is normalized per trial against a floored 2-s pre-cue rate and z-scored over all trials and bins (the Methods average each trial type and subtract its 10-s baseline), the screen and the normalization use rates floored to whole Hz, 0/0 suppression ratios are set to 1, the reward and cessation baseline is the 2 to 1 s before the event (the Methods say the 1 s before), and the waveform measure ('HD') is half the scale of Figure 3C.

The 95% bootstrap CIs printed for Figure 1G are not studentized intervals of the per-rat data (whose means and ANOVA match the paper exactly). They match the bootstrap-t quantiles added to the mean without reflection (for uncertainty minus safety [0.36, 1.03] against the paper's [0.35, 1.03]; the studentized interval is [-0.09, 0.59]). The CIs elsewhere may be formed the same way.

Question for the authors. Which normalization and which k-means run (starts, replicates, seed) produced the published populations, and can the population labels of the 193 units be deposited? The Methods' normalization does not give the paper's counts under any of the readings tried, and the attempt assumed the partition that best shows the five described patterns.

Question for the authors. How were the inter-trial interval events for reward and nose poke cessation chosen, given that the recording covers only 20 s before to about 33 s after each onset? The script's windows (pellets 18 to 2 s before or 14 to 28 s after onset; cessations 18 to 2 s before onset) and its baseline (2 to 1 s before the event) differ from the Methods' 1 s before; the attempt used events whose windows lie inside the recorded segments, with the Methods' baseline.

Question for the authors. How are 0/0 suppression ratios handled? The scripts set them to 1, which reproduces the paper's ANOVA; leaving them out or reading them as 0 changes the Figure 1G CIs and the Figure 1H danger correlation.

entries.name: crcns-nac-1-ray-2022
entries.title: Threat and bidirectional valence signaling in the nucleus accumbens core (Ray et al. 2022)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Ray, Moaddab and McDannald (2022) on CRCNS data set nac-1, which holds 368 nucleus accumbens core single units recorded from seven female rats during Pavlovian fear discrimination, with the session's cue, shock, pellet and nose poke times. It tests the behavior during recording, the cue-responsive screen, the k-means populations, their firing and waveform characteristics, cue firing, firing similarity, tuning curves, the fear output and exaggerated threat regressions, and reward and nose poke cessation firing. The pre-surgery sessions and the paper's population labels are not in the data set.
